newsitem.title: PERU: Peru rebels keeping officials as bargaining chip.
newsitem.headline: Peru rebels keeping officials as bargaining chip.

text.p: Peruvian Marxist rebels vowed on Sunday night to continue holding scores of hostages "linked to the regime" until President Alberto Fujimori agreed to release their jailed comrades.

"We ratify that the liberty of the authorities who today remain prisoners will only be possible if the government frees the comrades," said a guerrilla statement read by the first of a stream of hostages to be released on Sunday night.
Fujimori has flatly rejected the release of any of the more than 400 Tupac Amaru Revolutionary Movement (MRTA) guerrillas held in Peruvian jails.

The MRTA statement said the remaining government-linked hostages -- after the release of 225 as "a Christmas gesture" -- included ministers, vice-ministers, members of the judiciary, legislators, armed forces and police leaders and representatives of Japanese businesses.
Additionally, the rebels decided to hold some Asian and Latin American diplomats, "whose exit we shall be evaluating," the statement added.
The release of 225 captives left about 140 hostages still inside the Japanese ambassador's residence according to the Red Cross. The rebels stormed the residence on Tuesday night.
The rebels, whose statement was read by former government minister and released captive Sandro Fuentes, added:

"If Mr. Fujimori decides on a military solution, he will always find a Tupac Amaru member ready to remain vigilant in the defence of the interests of the people, defending our rights to work and the right to life of our brothers in the struggle."

The MRTA said that it sought a way out of the crisis "peacefully and respectful of our people's feeling." It criticised Fujimori for both his hard-hitting message to the nation on Saturday and his decision to cut basic services to the residence after it was taken over.
In the message, the MRTA claimed it existed to fight poverty.

"The MRTA was born in the country to struggle for the problems that marginalize the large majority of Peruvians, especially in the period of the government of President Alberto Fujimori that also worsened and increased poverty dramatically in Peru," it said.
